insights.insight: The network has produced 17,273 cryptographically verified receipts spanning physical retail, dining, fuel, warehouse, and digital SaaS — each one a confirmed transaction, not a behavioral inference. At $1.07M in verified GMV, the addressable signal pool is small but deterministic in a way no cookie-based or panel-based data source can match.

insights.topic: Receipt vs. probabilistic targeting cost gap
insights.insight: Display advertising pays $5+ CPM to infer purchase intent from browsing behavior; a verified receipt confirms a purchase already happened. That gap — probabilistic inference versus cryptographic proof — is the core pricing inefficiency brands should be evaluating as cookie deprecation removes the inferential layer entirely.

Google entered the top brand list on April 28, and SaaS subscriptions were first observed April 9 — signaling that verified receipt data is no longer confined to physical retail. For brands running digital acquisition campaigns, this opens the possibility of closing-loop measurement across both online and offline purchase confirmation.

Weekly GMV has compressed from a $211K peak on April 13 to a $66K–$81K operating band as of April 30, with velocity hitting a record low of 0.642x. The signal pool is growing but at a reduced pace; brands evaluating this data source should size expectations against current run-rate, not peak-week figures.

The network hit 29 active metros on April 19 — up from 25 on April 13 — with a single-heartbeat 17-CBSA expansion recorded at the $1M crossing. For marketers who need regional or local purchase verification, the footprint is widening, though concentration by market has not been disclosed.

Receipt inflow peaks consistently in the 16:15–20:15 window and troughs at 00:15 as prior-week volume rolls off — a repeatable pattern confirmed across multiple days. Marketers building real-time activation workflows on top of verified purchase data should account for this cadence when setting attribution windows or trigger logic.
